narrative.title: The Uniform-Hop Relay Distances
narrative.scenario: A packet relay mesh links routers with identical one-tick links. From the master router, ops needs each router's minimum tick count — the hop distance across the mesh — with unreachable routers flagged -1. Because every link costs exactly one tick, a level-by-level wave is sufficient; no weighted machinery required.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer N (vertices 0..N-1), the edge count M, an edge list edges, and the source vertex src.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an array where entry i is the minimum hop count from src to vertex i, or -1 if unreachable.

testCases.explanation: Wave rings: 0 first, 1 and 3 at one hop, 2 and 4 at two, 5 at three.
Vertices 2 and 3 live on an island the wave never crosses.

hintLevels: Level 1: Equal link costs make BFS rings the distances themselves.
Level 2: Track distance on enqueue — first arrival is the minimum for unit edges.
Level 3: Initialize with -1 and overwrite on first touch; untouched entries stay -1 for free.
